hints.title: Eliminate the linear variable
hints.body: The equation x+y=a gives y=a−x. Substitute this whole expression for y in 3x2+2xy=4.
hints.recap: Use the linear equation to reduce simultaneous equations to one variable.
hints.pitfall: The product becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, so both terms in the bracket are multiplied by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Expand and collect to form a quadratic in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Use the linear equation to substitute for one variable in the quadratic equation.

hints.title: Test for distinct real roots
hints.body: For the quadratic you obtain, form its discriminant in terms of the parameter and decide when it is strictly positive.
hints.recap: A nondegenerate quadratic has two distinct real roots precisely when its discriminant is positive.
hints.pitfall: Check the coefficient of the squared variable before applying the quadratic test.
hints.pause: Simplify your discriminant and determine the full parameter set.

recall.reminder: A nondegenerate quadratic has two distinct real roots precisely when its discriminant is positive.

solution:
Substitute y=a−x into the first equation: 3x2+2x(a−x)=4. Collecting terms gives x2+2ax−4=0.

The discriminant is (2a)2−4(1)(−4)=4a2+16>0 for every real a. The coefficient of x2 is always nonzero, and each root gives one y=a−x.

There are two distinct real x-values for all real a: G.
knowledgePattern: Eliminate a variable and test the discriminant for every parameter
